steps.title: Short Steps
steps.explanation: To find \( f'(-2) \) for the function \( f(x) = -3x^4 + x^3 - x^2 - 6x - 6 \), we first need to compute the derivative of \( f(x) \). The derivative of a polynomial is found by applying the power rule, which states that the derivative of \( x^n \) is \( nx^{n-1} \). Applying this rule to each term in \( f(x) \), we get: \[ f'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}(-3x^4) + \frac{d}{dx}(x^3) + \frac{d}{dx}(-x^2) + \frac{d}{dx}(-6x) + \frac{d}{dx}(-6) \]
